text:
mike: Heads up — our Ruby client started returning 401s in CI after I rotated the API key. Local runs are fine. Any quick ideas?

jess: Did you inspect the Authorization header in the failing job? GH Actions masks secrets so most prints become ***.

mike: I tried dumping headers with `set -x` and a curl dump, but the workflow output showed masked values. Running the same curl on my Mac works.

sam: Classic newline/encoding gotcha. How are you generating the Basic header in Ruby?

mike: In lib/redwood/client.rb we do:```ruby
auth = Base64.encode64("#{ENV['REDWOOD_API_KEY']}:")
headers['Authorization'] = "Basic #{auth}"
```

lara: There's the culprit — `Base64.encode64` inserts newline characters. Use `Base64.strict_encode64` (no newlines) or strip newline after encode.

sam: Also watch out for how the key is read into the env: `echo $KEY | base64` adds a newline unless you use `echo -n` or `printf '%s'`. In PowerShell use `-NoNewline`. On mac `pbcopy`/`pbpaste` can add a trailing newline depending on invocation.

mike: Ah, that matches. In my local tests I used `echo -n \"$KEY\" | base64`, but the CI step used an action that did `echo \"$KEY\" | base64` (no -n). So the header ended up with an extra byte.

jess: And GH Actions masking makes it confusing — when you `echo $SECRET` you see `***` so you think the value is non-empty but you can't see whitespace. For debugging, consider printing `echo -n \"$SECRET\" | wc -c` to get a length (masked value still shows stars but length reveals newline).

mike: Reproduced locally: `echo \"$KEY\" | base64` -> `abcd...\n` vs `echo -n \"$KEY\" | base64` -> `abcd...` (no newline). Switching to `Base64.strict_encode64("#{ENV['REDWOOD_API_KEY']}:")` fixed it. CI job green now.

lara: Quick checklist for everyone: use `Base64.strict_encode64` in Ruby, `echo -n` or `printf '%s'`, PowerShell `-NoNewline`, trim env vars in container entrypoints, and beware CRLF if editing .env on Windows.

infra-bot: Rotation complete — old key revoked at 2024-11-03T14:02:00Z :lock:

sam: TL;DR: newline added by encoding/shell caused malformed Basic header -> 401. Fix: strict base64 or strip newline.

mike: Thanks folks — I'll open a tiny PR to change encode64 -> strict_encode64 and add a unit test that constructs the header and asserts no "\n" in the value.

jess: Ping me for review, I can merge + ship a patch release fast.

mike: Will do.
